stories.headline: Anthropic starts its IPO roadshow, aiming to raise up to $64 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation
stories.why_read: This would be one of the largest listings ever, and it puts a public price on the company behind the coding model most developers now default to. The filing also shows how much compute the frontier really costs.
body: Anthropic is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, which could raise about $64.4 billion and value the company at roughly $1.4 trillion fully diluted. Alongside the public offering, Google and Microsoft plan a $26 billion private buy-in.

Revenue is described as running in the tens of billions, backed by about $900 billion in compute commitments. The risk factors call out customer concentration and a governance setup that leaves the founders with 50.1% of voting control, and skeptics are already questioning the company's timeline claims for curing disease.

stories.headline: Tesla now has more registered robotaxis in Texas than Waymo, 1,302 to 1,297
stories.why_read: This is your home state and the Cybercab is a big part of the count. A five-month swing from a 422-vehicle deficit says the Austin buildout is real, even if registrations aren't rides.
body: State records as of November 10 show Tesla with 1,302 registered robotaxis in Texas, made up of 729 Model Ys and 573 Cybercabs, edging past Waymo's 1,297. On September 1 Waymo led by 422 vehicles, and in June Tesla had just 59.

The caveat matters: registrations don't tell you how many cars are actively giving rides, and Waymo still leads nationally. But Tesla closed the Texas gap in about five months, where Waymo's presence took years to build, and it lands a day after Tesla said Giga Texas will drop the Cybertruck to focus on Cybercab.

stories.headline: Anthropic says its Mythos model ported Claude to AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days
stories.why_read: Porting a frontier model to a new accelerator used to take dozens of engineers and six to twelve months. If agents can do it in days, Nvidia's software moat gets a lot shallower.
body: Anthropic used Mythos to write nearly all of the code needed to get Claude running with usable performance on AMD's MI355X GPUs, in roughly three days. The company says this kind of port traditionally takes a large team the better part of a year.

It fits Anthropic's strategy of moving workloads across chips from Amazon, Google, Nvidia and now AMD for efficiency. The company credits that flexibility with helping revenue grow 45 times while compute costs rose only 10 times over six quarters.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model yet, with a 1M-token context window
stories.why_read: Two days after Claude 5.2, Google answers with a reasoning and software engineering model of its own. If you route agents between providers, the leaderboard just moved again.
body: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon on November 10, pitching it for deep reasoning, software engineering, science and cybersecurity, with a 1-million-token context window and top benchmark scores. It follows the earlier Argon release.

Leaks and code references point to faster, cheaper siblings on the way, Hydrogen as a Flash tier and Helix as Flash-Lite. Early users are sharing detailed 3D generations from temporary free access, alongside complaints about tight free-tier limits.

stories.headline: Stripe closes its roughly $7.5 billion purchase of OpenRouter
stories.why_read: You track OpenRouter's leaderboard every Monday, and now it belongs to a payments company. Watch for billing and routing to merge into one developer surface.
body: Stripe completed the acquisition on Tuesday after announcing it in August at around $7.5 billion to over $8 billion. OpenRouter serves more than 10 million developers and companies and routes over 10 trillion tokens a day across 400-plus models based on price, speed and reliability.

Patrick Collison pointed to usage now growing 125% in tokens per week and said Stripe plans to integrate OpenRouter's capabilities. The open question is how neutral a model router stays once it sits inside a company that wants to sell the payments layer for agents.

stories.headline: Regulators approve four advanced nuclear reactors at a Dow chemical plant on the Texas coast
stories.why_read: You reposted this one. It's the first such construction permit in over half a century, and it's industrial heat for a chemical plant, not just grid power, right here in Texas.
body: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission issued a construction permit on November 9 to Long Mott Energy, a Dow subsidiary, for four X-energy Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled reactors at Dow's Seadrift site in Calhoun County. They would supply high-temperature steam for chemical manufacturing plus excess electricity, about 320 megawatts electric in total, replacing aging natural gas systems.

NRC Chairman Ho K. Nieh called it America's first such permit in over 50 years, finished on an 18-month review. Construction could start later this decade if Dow makes its final investment decision by 2027, with startup aimed at the early 2030s.

stories.headline: A scan finds 35,578 Grok Build apps open to anyone with the link, some holding medical and contractor data
stories.why_read: You build with Grok Bot daily, so this is a direct reminder to check sharing defaults. The leak came from a default setting, not a hack.
body: Security firm Claroc scanned more than 43,000 grok.me app addresses and found 35,578 still reachable without login, many built from simple chat prompts with the default 'Anyone with the link' setting left on.

Exposed data spanned more than 30 organizations, including 3,784 worker medical exams, a U.S. Navy contractor roster of 108 people, Tesla scorecards, hospital staff lists, and SpaceXSI onboarding guides and sales maps. SpaceXSI pulled its 24 apps after media contact.

stories.headline: Apple is building Harbor, an app that pools Macs over Thunderbolt 5 into a private AI inference server
stories.why_read: Running open-weight models on a Mac Studio cluster has been a hobbyist project. A first-party app with no command line would make it a normal office purchase.
body: Leaker Aaron Perris found a new Apple app called Harbor that turns a Mac into a private inference server for open-weight models on Apple silicon, with nothing sent to the cloud. It detects other Thunderbolt 5 Macs and pools their unified memory into one cluster, so you can run models bigger than any single machine or serve more concurrent requests.
Harbor promises setup in minutes, in-app model browsing and downloads, and no infrastructure expertise. It's currently in private preview under Apple's Claris brand, per 9to5Mac.

stories.headline: Nvidia releases Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-billion-parameter open driving model for DRIVE AGX Thor
stories.why_read: A useful counterpoint to Tesla's end-to-end approach: a small, open model that reasons only when the scene gets hard. The at-fault numbers are worth a look.
body: Announced November 10, Alpamayo 2 Edge takes camera feeds, motion data and navigation and predicts 6.4 seconds ahead with low latency. It uses adaptive reasoning, saving compute on routine driving while working through complex cases like making room for a bus.
Nvidia says early tests reached 9.87 kilometers between at-fault incidents, 40 times better than baselines, and the weights are open.

stories.headline: Unplugged Performance offers to take over Cybertruck production at Giga Texas at no cost to Tesla
stories.why_read: A day after Tesla said the Cybertruck line ends, an Austin-area tuner wants to keep it alive. It's an unusual idea, and a local one.
body: Unplugged Performance proposed running the Cybertruck line at Gigafactory Texas, funded by its own investors, while giving Cybercab battery needs priority. Tesla would get license fees plus FSD and Robotaxi revenue shares.

The pitch includes the original Cybertruck, a three-row CyberSUV and an unmanned CyberCargo hauler, with plans to hire near Giga Texas and support Tesla's autonomy goals, including Optimus integration. Tesla hasn't publicly responded.

stories.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 now handles 75% of turns in T3 Code, and Musk says Grok 5 should pass it in two or three months
stories.why_read: Real usage data on which coding model people actually pick, plus a rare admission from Musk that Grok isn't there yet. You bookmarked the Musk reply.
body: In T3 Code, Theo Browne's free app for running coding agents side by side, Opus 5.5 handled 75% of user-started turns over the last seven days, up from 52% before its release and 64% the week after. Codex holds the rest, and some developers still mix tools for its speed.

Asked how Grok compares, Elon Musk replied: 'Not as good. Opus 5.5 is a masterpiece. But Grok 5 should exceed Opus 5.5 and maybe that happens in 2 or 3 months, with continued acceleration thereafter.'

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Whiteboards and Sheets in beta, and Dashboards goes GA as Claude Data
stories.why_read: Claude keeps eating the office suite. Certified queries in Claude Data are the piece an architect should notice: one blessed definition of each metric.
body: Whiteboards is a shared board where a team brainstorms with Claude, which can turn a spoken plan into a timeline with owners and dates or group retro notes by theme. Sheets builds and edits spreadsheets with tabs, formulas and drop-downs, flagging each edit, with export to .xlsx or CSV.

Claude Dashboards, in beta since October, is now generally available as Claude Data, querying sources like Redshift, BigQuery and ClickHouse. Certified queries and live sharing are in beta. All three are on paid plans, with hand-offs to Miro, Lucid, Airtable, Asana and others.

stories.headline: VulnCheck counts 442 CVEs from Anthropic's Glasswing in seven months, with only 217 findings marked fixed
stories.why_read: A data-driven check on one of AI's loudest security claims. The gap between finding bugs and getting them fixed is now the real story.
body: Seven months into Project Glasswing, VulnCheck has tracked 442 CVEs attributable to Anthropic, about 0.5% of all CVEs this year, and only two exploited in the wild. Of 37,966 reported findings, 7,349 are public and just 217 are marked fixed; Anthropic added nearly 12,000 findings since September with only 15 more fixes.

About 1,654 findings are duplicates and 419 were withdrawn, while Anthropic's claimed true-positive rate rose to 94.2%. The post says the scanner shifts validation work onto maintainers: curl rejected 19 of 34 published reports as vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 hits 96% success picking brackets on live Mercedes-Benz lines
stories.why_read: Robots on real production lines, not demos. Pair it with Nvidia's GR00T 2 from yesterday and physical AI had a big week.
body: Announced November 10, Gemini Robotics 2.5 handles more than 200 everyday and industrial tasks, from pipetting liquids to folding laundry and automotive kitting, with 30% to 100% higher success rates and 20% to 30% faster completion.
With Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz, Apollo 2 robots reached a 96% success rate picking and organizing metal brackets on active production lines in Hungary and Germany.

stories.headline: SpaceX orders a €60 million solar cell line for its Bastrop factory to power orbital AI satellites
stories.why_read: Orbital data centers sound like science fiction until someone buys the production line. This one is in Bastrop, just outside Austin.
body: SpaceX signed a €60 million contract with Germany's SINGULUS TECHNOLOGIES for a turnkey line making heterojunction solar cells at its Bastrop, Texas factory, starting in early 2027.

The cells are for Starmind satellites, orbital data centers with large solar arrays feeding up to 250 kW of AI compute, linked back by Starlink lasers. The deal could grow to equipment for more than 100 GW of cells a year.

stories.headline: FCC accepts SpaceX's bid to buy low-band spectrum covering every American for Starlink phone service
stories.why_read: This is how direct-to-phone satellite coverage becomes nationwide. Low-band spectrum is what reaches indoors and out in the country.
body: The FCC accepted SpaceX's application to buy 546 paired licenses from Grain Management, covering 100% of the U.S. population with up to 14 MHz of low-band spectrum. With existing holdings, SpaceX would have up to 89 MHz in many markets for a hybrid satellite-and-ground network.
A Qualcomm deal will equip thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. Public comments are due December 1, and final approval is still needed.

stories.headline: Starlink Mini 2 adds a quick-swap battery good for up to 4.5 hours of internet
stories.why_read: From your bookmarks, and on the HN front page. Satellite internet with no outlet at all is a real change for travel and emergencies.
body: SpaceX's new Starlink Mini 2 has a quick-swap battery that delivers up to 4.5 hours of service on a single charge, so the dish can run in the middle of nowhere without plugging into anything.
The product page drew more than 400 points on Hacker News, where the discussion covers battery life, power draw and how it compares with the first Mini.

stories.headline: Tesla starts earthworks on Project Crystal Sun, a $10.1 billion solar factory in Fort Bend County, Texas
stories.why_read: Another Texas megaproject, and this one makes everything from silicon ingots to finished panels. It's Tesla's energy business getting serious about supply.
body: Tesla has begun major site preparation for a vertically integrated solar plant covering ingots, wafers, cells and finished panels. The $10.1 billion facility was approved earlier this year with local support.
It targets completion in 2028 and operations by early 2029, with a promised 9,712 permanent jobs and a projected $107 billion boost to Texas GDP.

stories.headline: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN ship Modern Web Guidance to stop coding agents writing 2019-era JavaScript
stories.why_read: You reposted the Edge team's announcement. It's a skill pack your agents can install today to stop reaching for heavy polyfills and JS where CSS will do.
body: Modern Web Guidance is a set of agent skills that put web platform best practices and browser-compatibility data straight into a coding agent's context. It's stewarded by the Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN teams, and ships plugins for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini and others.

The pitch: models default to legacy patterns because their training data is full of old code. The CLI can search guides, retrieve one by ID, or run a legacy-scan over a codebase, and the guides are pruned by evals to stay token-efficient.

stories.headline: A former Meta engineer lists four ways AI-generated code makes a codebase fragile
stories.why_read: Nearly 600 HN points and a useful checklist if your team now generates most of its code. Shallow tests are the one to audit first.
body: Evan Merz says he generated at least 90% of his code with AI at Meta and now writes 100% that way at another large company, but he argues the result is brittle at scale. AI handles what fits in its context window and misses longer-term issues.

His four failure modes: shallow tests that pad coverage without covering what matters, overly complex code with too many helpers, falling human understanding of the codebase, and the long-term debt that follows. It pairs well with Gergely Orosz's argument, which you bookmarked, that fast AI implementation may bring back big upfront planning.

stories.headline: Airbnb open-sources Skipper, its embedded workflow engine, under Apache 2.0
stories.why_read: You reposted this. An embedded workflow engine from a company running at Airbnb's scale is worth a look before you reach for another orchestration service.
body: Airbnb Engineering announced that Skipper, its embedded workflow engine, is now on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license.
Embedded means it runs inside your service rather than as a separate orchestration platform, which is the trade-off to weigh against tools like Temporal for your own systems.

stories.headline: eMudhra's incident report says a Python script truncated its CA private keys to one byte
stories.why_read: You reposted Scott Helme on this. It's a rare, concrete look at how a certificate authority can break the rules everyone's TLS depends on.
body: Scott Helme flagged that certificate authority eMudhra's incident report is out, and that a Python script truncated the CA's private keys to a single byte.
Helme added that the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements cover key export and import (section 6.2.6) and storage on the HSM (6.2.7), and that eMudhra broke both with how it handled the keys.

stories.headline: Lenny Rachitsky's job market report: PMs are winning in the AI era, engineering demand has stalled
stories.why_read: You reposted it. Twice-yearly hiring data is one of the few hard signals on how AI is reshaping tech roles.
body: In his fifth twice-yearly look at hiring and job openings, Lenny Rachitsky calls this one the most surprising yet.
His headline findings: product managers are winning in the AI era, engineering demand has stalled, and design openings are at a record low.

stories.headline: Chips and Cheese takes apart AMD's Zen 6: cheaper branch misses and both decode clusters for one thread
stories.why_read: If you size servers, this is the clearest read on what next year's EPYC cores change. AMD reworked more than the version number suggests.
body: George Cozma finds Zen 6 looks like an evolution of Zen 5 from above, but AMD reworked several parts of the core, much like the Zen 1 to Zen 2 jump. The integer schedulers return to a layout reminiscent of Zen 3 and Zen 4.

The branch predictor keeps Zen 5's accuracy but recovers faster from a wrong guess, roughly 3 to 3.5 ns per mispredict versus 3.5 to 4 ns. And unlike Zen 5, a single thread can now use both decode clusters.

stories.headline: Tendrils raises $30 million from Benchmark to build a CPU with thousands of parallel cores
stories.why_read: A clean-sheet bet against decades of backward compatibility, with its own language to match. Long odds, but the right question for AI-era compute.
body: Tendrils argues today's CPUs are held back by cache coherency protocols and reorder buffers inherited from sequential, single-core designs. Its processor instead targets thousands of cores in parallel, moving past shared mutable memory and linear instruction streams.
It's co-developing Vine, an open-source language built for parallel-first hardware. Benchmark led the round with the UK Sovereign AI Fund, Conviction and others, and Jack Altman joins the board.

stories.headline: A hacker voltage-glitches a cheap mining card into an A100-80G that runs about 1.2 times faster than retail
stories.why_read: A great hardware security read, and a reminder that fuses are only as strong as the voltage rail around them.
body: Kate found a voltage fault injection flaw on Nvidia's GA100 die that lets an operator blow arbitrary fuses. She used it to turn a CMP 170HX mining card into what is effectively an A100 with 80GB, and it benchmarks about 1.18 times a retail A100 in FP16 because all functional SMs, around 120 to 126, are enabled instead of the yield-safe 108.
Features disabled on the mining card, like NVLink and PCIe Gen4, can be unlocked the same way, though she hasn't tested all of them yet.

stories.headline: Val Town is winding down after four years, and will open-source the platform in February
stories.why_read: A well-loved scripting platform admits it couldn't compete in cloud computing. If you have vals running, the read-only date is December 10.
body: Founder Steve Krouse says Val Town couldn't compete in the cloud computing space. New signups stopped November 10, billing is paused, and annual prepaid plans get partial refunds.
Vals go read-only on December 10, other services end January 10, and the code will be open-sourced February 1, 2027. The team published migration guides for Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Render.

stories.headline: How to keep SSH keys in your Mac's Secure Enclave, so the private key never touches disk
stories.why_read: You just set up SSH commit signing on your own machine. This is the next step: keys that can't be copied even if the laptop is compromised.
body: Since macOS Sequoia, a Mac can create SSH keys inside the Secure Enclave with the built-in sc_auth tool, optionally requiring Touch ID for every signature. The disk holds only a reference that is useless on any other machine.
Serge Gatezh walks through the native setup and compares it with Secretive, a YubiKey, and 1Password or Bitwarden agents. He found the native route fully works but too clunky to live with day to day.

stories.headline: Terence Tao's Six Math Essentials is out, a 128-page tour from numbers to dynamics
stories.why_read: Math from one of the best living mathematicians, written for everyone. A good one to read or gift.
body: Fields Medalist Terence Tao's new book walks through six ideas: numbers as the gateway to quantitative thinking, algebra as abstraction, geometry, probability for reasoning under uncertainty, analysis for taming the very large and very small, and dynamics as the math of change.
The U.S. hardcover from Quanta Books went on sale November 10; the UK edition, Six Maths Essentials: How to Model the World, came out in October from Pelican.

stories.headline: Foldable Flight collects the world's best paper airplanes, including a 31.2-second time-aloft record holder
stories.why_read: The top-voted page on HN today is pure joy. Pick one, fold it, and fly it with the kids.
body: The site has more than 100 designs you can filter by difficulty, plane type and paper size, each rated for speed, glide and accuracy. Unite holds the world record for time aloft at 31.2 seconds, and the Firefly prototype can fly over 300 feet.
Easier picks include the Arrowhead, whose tutorials have more than 100 million views, and the Quick Blade, which flies over 100 feet.
